purpose: Translate the Feb air-capability correction and Japanese regeneration feedback into the current dormant Bengal/Arakan posture without reopening a land offensive or Eastern Fleet chase.

Japan.theater_air_state: 5th Air Division is healthier and less centrally sucked into Imphal than historical; Bengal/Arakan can retain a meaningful western pool.
not_automatically_credited: deep maritime search comparable to 705 G4M

Allies.meaning: Chittagong loss displaced the group and cost aircraft/infrastructure but did not destroy the formation; northern fields and India-wide maintenance/training depth sustain a substantial counterweight.

land_effect: Air balance becomes more active and costly but not decisive. Japanese air can make Feni/Comilla buildup and daylight movement harder; Allied air can contest Patenga/LOC. Neither side gains a ground offensive automatically because Japanese coastal throughput/55th Division recovery and Allied re-equipment/logistics remain independent gates.
naval_effect: Eastern Fleet dormancy judgment is unchanged. Stronger Bengal IJA air is predominantly tactical/recon rather than the long-range maritime strike system required to chase a conserved Eastern Fleet at Ceylon. Submarines remain the cheaper naval pressure tool.
reopen_trigger_effect: If either side later approves a land offensive, use these larger air pools and re-run local sortie allocation rather than resurrecting the older 70-105/115-155 bands.
supersedes_interpretation: Bengal_Arakan_No224_Group_branch_reconstituted bands inside the same v002 ledger
